BCRA reports positive net result of USD 2.5 billion from gold position in 2025
The Central Bank of Argentina reported a positive net gain of USD 2.505 billion from its gold holdings for fiscal year 2025. Officials outlined their longstanding use of financial hedges and addressed recent criticism from audit authorities.
The Central Bank of the Argentine Republic announced on Oct. 8 that its gold position yielded a positive net result of USD 2.505 billion during the 2025 fiscal year. The outcome reflects both the evolution of gold prices and financial hedging operations routinely applied to all its holdings in this asset.
The bank said that the financial operations with gold recorded in 2025 are part of its hedging policy, which aims to protect international reserves against potential losses from significant declines in one of its main assets' value. The strategy covers 100% of its gold position.
According to the statement, such hedging instruments come at a cost. "In years when gold performs favorably — as was the case in 2025 — derivative instruments acting as insurance typically record a negative result," the bank said. It added that this is due to the nature of hedging: while gains are seen on the underlying asset, protective instruments absorb losses, so both sides must be considered together for an accurate assessment.
The bank also noted that these practices have been standard since 2007, and between 2007 and 2011 payments for similar coverage were nearly double those made in 2025 relative to market value. During this earlier period, neither Argentina's National Audit Office nor external auditors raised concerns about these strategies or related payments.
The National Audit Office approved BCRA’s financial statements for fiscal year 2025, which saw record results and the highest increase in equity over two decades. However, BCRA criticized recent actions by audit officials as politically motivated attempts to discredit central bank leadership, saying: "It is clear from their latest communication where they refer to these transactions as coverage but later summarize them as speculative." The central bank said it remains focused on upholding high standards and building on strong results achieved over the past quarter century.
